definitions.gloss: errand; task of going somewhere on behalf of someone
definitions.explanation: The act of being sent to do something, especially delivering a message or purchasing something on someone's behalf.
A person sent to deliver a message, carry out a task, or serve as a representative.

examples.japanese: お{使|つか}いに{行|い}ってきて。
examples.english: Go run an errand for me.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}がひとりでお{使|つか}いに{行|い}けるようになった。
examples.english: The child became able to go on errands by themselves.

examples.japanese: {母|はは}に{頼|たの}まれて、スーパーへお{使|つか}いに{行|い}った。
examples.english: My mother asked me to go, so I ran an errand to the supermarket.

examples.japanese: {神|かみ}の{使|つか}いとされる{動物|どうぶつ}がいる。
examples.english: There are animals considered to be divine messengers.

examples.japanese: {王|おう}は{使|つか}いを{送|おく}って{和平|わへい}を{申|もう}し{入|い}れた。
examples.english: The king sent an envoy to propose peace.

examples.japanese: {奈良|なら}では{鹿|しか}が{春日大社|かすがたいしゃ}の{神|かみ}の{使|つか}いとして{大切|たいせつ}にされている。
examples.english: In Nara, deer are treasured as divine messengers of Kasuga Grand Shrine.

notes:
The noun form of {使|つか}う (to use), but with specialized meanings. The most common everyday usage is お{使|つか}い (with the polite prefix お), meaning an errand — especially a child being sent to buy something at a shop.

The TV show "はじめてのおつかい" (My First Errand) is a beloved long-running Japanese program that follows young children on their first solo shopping trips.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- お{使|つか}いに{行|い}く: to go on an errand
- お{使|つか}いを{頼|たの}む: to ask someone to run an errand
- {神|かみ}の{使|つか}い: divine messenger
- {使|つか}いを{出|だ}す: to send a messenger

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {用事|ようじ}: errand, business to attend to — more general, can be any task or appointment
- {使者|ししゃ}: messenger, envoy — a more formal synonym for the "messenger" sense
- {買|か}い{物|もの}: shopping — focuses on the purchasing aspect rather than being sent by someone
